# Notes of this project for coding agents

Dennis Otto: The projects of Dennis Otto in one place: Home Assistant, Nextcloud and Paperless, GitHub automation and the blueprint they all share.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- `.github/mkdocs_project.py` is what MkDocs loads and what the scripts and the workflows run, and it stays thin: it passes the event hooks on and holds the options of the script. The code is in the package `.github/hub/`, a module for each concern, which the docstring of `.github/hub/__init__.py` lists in the order of their imports; a module imports only those above it and the standard library. `tests/test_mkdocs_project.py` asserts that list, and fails for a module over 750 lines: give its second concern a module of its own. Each module has its tests in `tests/test_hub_<module>.py`, such as those of the fix of the catalog bot in `tests/test_hub_fix.py`, and those of the real repository in `tests/test_hub_repository.py`; `tests/hub_helpers.py` holds what several of them share and `tests/conftest.py` the fixtures. All that asks the web goes through `.github/hub/web.py`, called as `web.download()`, so that a test replaces it in one place with `monkeypatch.setattr(hub.web, "download", ...)`. `mkdocs serve` builds again after a change of `projects.toml` or of a page, but only a new start reads a change of the package.
- `projects.toml` lists every project once; the hooks of the website turn it into the cards of both home pages, the tables of `README.md` and of the German `README.de.md`, with the German texts and addresses first, the files at the root of the address, and on the Trust pages the guarantees that every project shares, the table of the numbers of each project, which a phone shows as a card for each with `docs/stylesheets/extra.css`, and the tabs of verify commands in place of `<!-- trust-shared -->`, `<!-- trust -->` and `<!-- verify -->`, from the `[trust]` texts and the optional `asset` key of each project. `scripts/check-project.sh` runs their tests with every line and branch covered.
- The picture of a card has a file in each language, `image.en` and `image.de`, in `docs/images/projects/`. `scripts/project-pictures.sh` makes the English one from the social preview of the repository and draws the German one from `.github/card-picture.html`: `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --drawings FOLDER` writes a copy of that page for each with the texts of the project, and the script fetches the screenshot and the logo that `drawing` of `projects.toml` names beside it, and renders it with the Chromium of `scripts/social-preview.sh`. The placeholders of the page are those of `string.Template`, such as `${name}`, so the page holds no other `$`. The tests write the pages of the real catalog without the network or Docker; after a change of the page or of a `drawing`, run the script and look at the pictures. The pictures of the first group of the home page load at once, the first with `fetchpriority="high"`; `section()` gives each card how its picture loads.
- The line *Works with …* of a card comes from `requires` of its project in `projects.toml`: a text in every language, or a file of its repository, such as `hacs.json`, with the field of each value and a text with `{}`. The hooks read the file at the tag of the latest release of the build from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and take only a version from it, matched by `VERSION`; a file that can't be read leaves the line off without a warning, and the catalog bot reads the same file on the default branch. The tests read the files of the real projects from `tests/fixtures/requirements/`, never from the network: a new source in `projects.toml` needs its fixture there.
- The Releases page, `docs/releases.md` and `docs/releases.de.md`, gets the notes of the latest releases of every project in place of `<!-- release-notes -->`, and *What's new* of the home pages the latest release of each in place of `<!-- releases -->`: the hooks read them from the API of GitHub at the build and keep only text, lists, headings, tables, code and links to https of the notes, which take the place of their placeholders in `on_page_content`, after Markdown. The headline of *What's new* leaves out the scope of a commit, and a release whose pull requests are all of maintenance, by `INTERNAL` and `QUIET` of `.github/hub/releases.py`, shows `maintenance` of `[facts]` in the language of the page instead. The page keeps the notes for users alone, cut by `for_users` at the heading *Every pull request of this release* of the blueprint's release bot, while the headline and `maintenance` read all of the notes; `redate`, from `on_page_content` after every hook that dates a page by its Markdown, dates a page that shows the releases by the newest of them in the sitemap and in the date of its last change, and `--site` checks that date. Never let the HTML of a release reach a page another way; [decision 0005](../docs/decisions/0005-the-releases-page-takes-the-notes-from-the-api-at-the-build.md) says why.
- The fix of the catalog bot in `.github/hub/fix.py`, `--network repositories.json --fix pull-request.md`, makes the edits with one correct form, after the comparison of `.github/hub/bot.py`: `wanted_docs` asks the web for the address of a project in every language, and leaves a project to a person when a repository is gone, private or archived or when the web doesn't settle it; `with_docs` writes the lines of `DOCS_LINE` inside the `[[project]]` of its slug and returns `None` for any other form; `wanted_accent` takes for a `drawing.accent` that the social preview of its repository lacks the one `--accent` that the preview names, and leaves a preview without one, or with two different ones, to a person, and `with_accent` writes the line of `ACCENT_LINE` the same way; and `reads_back` holds an edit back unless the file reads as the wanted catalog, so a difference without an edit keeps its sentence in the issue. A new light changes no other file: the merge changes `projects.toml` on `main`, which `.github/screenshots-paths.txt` lists, so the screenshot bot draws the pictures anew. `healed_files` writes what follows an address: the tables of the READMEs, `tests/fixtures/not-found-data.json` and the links of `docs/*.md`. The bot's pull request must pass the checks, so no test may name a German website of the real catalog: take them from the catalog, as `GERMAN_SITES` does. The job *catalog-pull-request* of `.github/workflows/catalog.yml` has the release app, checks out only its script `scripts/catalog-pull-request.sh`, and commits only the paths that `edited` in that script lets through, so a new file of `healed_files` goes there too; `tests/test_catalog_pull_request.py` runs the script in bash against a fake gh on the `PATH` with the real jq, which `scripts/check-project.sh` leaves to the CI where jq is missing, so a change of its shell comes with a case there; it asks the app for contents, pull requests and workflows alone, and writes the issue with the token of the workflow. It enables no auto-merge: a person merges what the web asked for. Only a run on `main` changes the issues of the jobs *catalog* and *watch*; one from another branch writes its findings into the summary of the job alone.
- The watch of the catalog bot, `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --watch`, which the job *watch* of `.github/workflows/catalog.yml` runs every day, asks the live websites for what the hub depends on after its build: the data of the dashboard against `.github/dashboard-fields.json`, the search index of every project website, what the build made of the releases and of those indexes (the places `release-newer` of the Releases page, which name the releases that the build read, and the entries of every project website in the search index of the hub), the files at the root of the address and every old address of `former/`. Each finding is one sentence of the issue *The live websites need attention*, with what readers lose and the fix. `.github/dashboard-fields.json` names the schema of `repos.json` and the kind of every field that `docs/javascripts/projects.js` reads, one of `KINDS` of `.github/hub/watch.py`; `tests/projects.test.mjs` reads the data through a `Proxy` and fails when the script reads a field that the file doesn't name, so a change of what the script reads changes the file in the same pull request. The tests of the watch read `tests/fixtures/repos.json` and the files that the hooks write, never the network. The hooks also write the counts of the search into the summary of the job, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which the tests unset for every test.
- `scripts/check-site.sh`, which the check *docs* runs after the strict build with the folder `site`, runs `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --site site`: it checks in the built website what the hooks promise in the files that they alone write or change after the build, as the table in *The check of the built website* of `README.md` lists, and names each broken promise with its file and its fix. A hook that writes something new after the build gets its rule there too, with a test that breaks the folder of `hub_site` in `tests/test_hub_sitecheck.py`; `bash scripts/check.sh` builds the website without it, so run it yourself after `mkdocs build --strict`.
- `tests/e2e/hub.mjs`, which `scripts/check-site.sh` runs after its check of the files, uses the built website in Google Chrome with the `playwright-core` of `tests/e2e/package-lock.json`, in the light scheme at the width of a phone and of a desktop: each scenario of `SCENARIOS` has an `id`, which names its screenshot and trace in `site/.e2e/`, and a `title`, which `[check.docs]` of `.github/checks.project.toml` names one by one, as `tests/test_checks_project.py` asserts. It answers every request to the address from `site` as GitHub Pages does, with its `404.html` and the status 404 for a file that it lacks, the data of the dashboard from `tests/fixtures/repos.json` and a page of a project website with a stand-in, and refuses every other server. A part of the hub that only works in a browser, together with Material, gets a scenario there, with its title in `[check.docs]` and a row in the table of *The hub in a browser* of `README.md`. A scenario takes what it expects from the built website and the catalog, such as the word of the search from the index of the page, never a text that a change of a project website would break.
- A project whose repository was renamed names the old folders of its website in `former` of `projects.toml`, and the pages of each old website in `former/<folder>.txt`. The hooks write a page at every old address that leads to the same page in the new folder, the 404 page of `overrides/404.html` leads every other address of an old folder there, and the card keeps the old anchor; [decision 0004](../docs/decisions/0004-the-root-website-keeps-the-old-addresses-of-a-renamed-project.md) says why.
- `docs/javascripts/projects.js` writes the live facts of the dashboard into the cards of the home pages and the `td[data-fact]` cells of the Trust pages as they load, a release newer than the build into *What's new* and the Releases pages, and the day of every release as the time since; `overrides/facts.html` loads it on those pages. Its tests, `tests/projects.test.mjs`, run with Node 22.8 or newer and no packages, `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, on a document of their own; `scripts/check-project.sh` runs them with the tests of the hooks.
- The 404 page and every page run a script of their own inline: `overrides/partials/not-found.js`, which `overrides/404.html` includes with its data as the JSON of `#not-found-data`, and `overrides/partials/search-hold.js`, which `overrides/main.html` includes before the scripts of the theme. Write their code in those files, never in a template: Jinja reads them as part of the template, so they must hold no `{{`, `{%`, `{#` or end tag of a script, and `exclude_docs` of `mkdocs.yml` keeps them off the website as files. `tests/not-found.test.mjs` and `tests/search-hold.test.mjs` run them in `node:vm` with a page, an address and an `XMLHttpRequest` of their own; a script that the browser runs in place, without `module`, gets its tests there the same way, with the address of its file as the `filename` of `vm`, so that its coverage counts.
- `scripts/check-project.sh` fails when the tests of the scripts leave a line, a branch or a function of `docs/javascripts/*.js` or `overrides/partials/*.js` uncovered, with `--test-coverage-lines=100 --test-coverage-branches=100 --test-coverage-functions=100` of Node 22.8 or newer; Node measures only the files that a test loads, so `tests/scripts.test.mjs` fails for a script of those folders without a `tests/<name>.test.mjs` that reads it. A new script in another folder needs its `--test-coverage-include` there and in `tests/scripts.test.mjs`. `tests/fixtures/not-found-data.json` is the data of the 404 script for projects.toml today; a Python test keeps it equal to what the hooks write, so write it anew after a change of the catalog.
- The code follows the coding standards of *Coding standards* in `README.md`, which `scripts/check-project.sh` checks: the Python of the hooks, `scripts/screenshots.py` and the tests the format and the rules of Ruff in `ruff.toml` and the strict mode of mypy in `mypy.ini`, with the Ruff and the mypy of `requirements-test.txt`; the JavaScript of `docs/javascripts/`, `overrides/partials/` and `tests/` the format and the recommended rules of Biome in `biome.jsonc`, with the Biome of `tests/lint/package-lock.json`. `bash scripts/check-project.sh --fix` fixes what Ruff and Biome can, and is the autofix of the step, beside the command that writes the tables. Both tools leave the code of the blueprint alone, `.github/blueprint.py`, `.github/blueprint/`, `.github/mkdocs_blueprint.py` and the scripts in `.github/`, and Ruff every Markdown file, whose Python blocks it would format otherwise, as `tests/test_checks_project.py` asserts against `.github/blueprint/owned.txt`. A new Python file outside the folders of `files` in `mypy.ini` needs its path there, and a new folder of scripts for the browser its pattern in `includes` of `biome.jsonc` and in the override that keeps `"use strict"`, which Biome calls redundant because it takes every `.js` for a module, while the browser runs them as classic scripts. Biome breaks a line longer than 80 characters, so a test that reads code, such as `scenarios()` of `tests/test_checks_project.py`, reads it in either layout.
- `scripts/screenshots.sh` takes the pictures of the website for `README.md`, `README.de.md` and the About pages with `scripts/screenshots.py`, which runs in Playwright's image without a network and drives its headless Chromium through the DevTools protocol on the pipe of `--remote-debugging-pipe`, with the standard library of Python alone, since the image has no package of Playwright. `SHOTS` lists every picture: a new one is a line there, its place in `README.md` or a page, and its file in `tests/test_screenshots.py`, which runs the script with a Chromium of its own that answers on the pipe. A picture that only the READMEs show is named `website-*`, the German home page `website-*.de.webp`, which `exclude_docs` of `mkdocs.yml` keeps off the website. The About pages show the search in a `<picture>` for each color scheme, with `#only-light` or `#only-dark` and the still for reduced motion as its one source, because the hooks of the blueprint turn a `<picture>` with a source for each scheme into two pictures and drop every other source; their German pictures are `NAME.de.webp`, which MkDocs serves on the German pages at the address of the English ones.
